verdict: S4 not fully passing: two reproducible mobile failures; remaining partial evidence is explicitly distinguished from application defects.

statusDefinitions.pass_local: Expected local invariants covered by freshly exercised existing suites and/or supplemental browser/HTTP probes; does not imply deployment or every variant in one combined journey.
statusDefinitions.partial: Some evidence exists, but the named exact variant or external boundary has not been fully verified. This is not an assertion that the repository has no corresponding test.
statusDefinitions.fail: An expected outcome failed in an exercised real browser scenario.

environment.worker: local workerd / isolated D1 and R2

runs.interpretation: 30 existing tests plus 2 temporary scenarios. Two existing Storefront mobile tests fail with long-text stress catalog. Two initial temporary-fixture failures were corrected and are not application defects.

Cross-Store identity replacement passed. Business journey completed all three branches; its only final failures are three soft assertions recording the same 375-to-547 Console overflow. Primary color assertions passed.

covers: full unassigned/other-assigned processing denial matrix and additional Staff catalog routes
forged authority/malformed paths/SQL fragments/public Store forgery

runs.caveat: Raw customer-name search misses proposed <=1.25x relative budget (2x); absolute values are small. Staff reads 1500 vs Owner 26 rows on this sparse ordered search. Payment-reference search remains unmeasured. No full S4-15 pass claimed.

reproduction: Create an active Product with a valid long unbroken text segment, e.g. S4 <script>window.s4Injected=true</script> followed by a UUID.
Open Storefront at 375px. The script-like text is safely escaped but the title crosses the viewport.
Provision local Staff with a long valid Unicode name such as Nguyễn 東京 Staff followed by a UUID.
Assign a real Order to that Staff; open Owner Order detail at 375px with assignment/payment/refund content.
confirmedFailures.observedElement: .page-stack clientWidth 343, scrollWidth 531; assignment section and detail content extend beyond viewport
confirmedFailures.rootCauseBoundary: Actual overflow is proven. Exact leaf min-content constraint has not been isolated; no application CSS fix was made.
confirmedFailures.primaryActionColors: pass: enabled action matches color-accent fill and color-accent-ink text

scenarios.scenario: Existing Store A Owner signs in for the first time after S4 migration and opens an old paid Order and its history.
scenarios.expected: The same Store A records, IDs, snapshots, and payment evidence are accessible. Sign-in does not create a replacement Store or reseed data.
scenarios.assessment: Populated raw migration and preservation passed. No fresh browser login against that exact migrated paid-Order fixture was captured.

scenarios.scenario: New Store A Staff has no assignments, then Owner assigns one pending Order; Staff reloads Orders and Products.
scenarios.expected: Initially show an empty assigned inbox, not all Store Orders. After assignment show that Order and accurate totals; Products remain read-only.
scenarios.assessment: Real Staff starts with zero assignments and read-only Products; Owner assignment unlocks processing.

scenarios.scenario: A valid authenticated account has no membership, a removed membership, or a membership pointing to an unavailable Store.
scenarios.expected: Deny private access without bootstrap fallback or selecting the first Store. Do not create membership automatically from email or successful login.
scenarios.assessment: Absent, revoked and ambiguous membership paths are covered. Unavailable-Store membership variant was not independently exercised.

scenarios.scenario: Tutor provisioning attempts to reuse an existing login identity for a different Store/role, or a guest calls account-creation endpoints directly.
scenarios.expected: Provisioning must not silently repurpose or elevate an account. Public signup is disabled; credential identity alone never grants Store membership. Explicitly configured multi-membership, if supported, requires validated Store selection.
scenarios.assessment: Provisioning identity reuse/conflicts and disabled public account-creation paths passed existing suites and Node rehearsal.

scenarios.scenario: Assignment/decision requests contain missing IDs, nulls, malformed percent-encoding, unknown action strings, or unsupported extra fields.
scenarios.expected: Reject invalid commands with bounded errors and no assignment, decision, or audit mutation. Follow existing error contracts; never reinterpret missing Store identity as Store A.
scenarios.assessment: Extra HTTP probes rejected null/missing/forged assignment bodies, malformed encoded paths and unknown decision action; full decision-body variant matrix was not separately replayed.

scenarios.scenario: A person name, Product title, or existing Refund reason contains long Unicode text, bidirectional characters, or the maximum supported length.
scenarios.expected: Render safe text without breaking controls or 375 px layout. Preserve existing valid data; enforce declared limits on new input without inventing arbitrary truncation.
scenarios.assessment: Valid long Product text overflows Storefront: viewport 375, document 430. Console stress content also overflows. Payload renders as text, not script.

scenarios.scenario: Staff submits Owner role, another actor ID, Store A ID while signed into B, or approved status inside a normal Order-edit payload.
scenarios.expected: Authority comes exclusively from verified identity/membership and the named domain action. Reject unsupported authority/state fields; no mass-assignment bypass.
scenarios.assessment: Forged authority fields on assignment and forged public storeId were rejected without writes. Not every Store-B/Staff mutation variant was replayed.

scenarios.scenario: Attacker supplies SQL fragments in IDs/search/cursors and HTML/script payloads in names or Refund reasons, then views them in both apps.
scenarios.expected: Treat query values as data and rendered content as text. No broadened result scope, executed script, leaked session, or state change from malformed input.
scenarios.assessment: SQL-fragment ID/search probes did not widen visibility; HTML/script names and reasons did not execute in either real app. SQL-fragment cursor variant not independently replayed.

scenarios.scenario: Staff A1 loads an assigned Order, Owner reassigns it to A2, and A1 submits fulfillment while the reassignment is committing.
scenarios.expected: Use a coherent atomic ordering: A1 may succeed only if its authorized mutation commits before reassignment. Once reassignment wins, A1 cannot mutate; no read-check/unconditional-write gap.
scenarios.assessment: Commit-boundary assignment-loss guards pass. Exact two-client A1-to-A2 reassignment racing fulfillment was not independently captured.

scenarios.scenario: Two Owner sessions submit Approve and Reject for the same pending Refund Request concurrently using different command keys.
scenarios.expected: Exactly one decision and one decision audit event persist. The conflicting request fails without overwriting the winner; Order/payment state does not change.
scenarios.assessment: Concurrent opposite final decisions and atomic single-winner ledger/history tests passed.

scenarios.scenario: A decision commits but its response is lost; the Owner retries the same command repeatedly, then reuses its key with a different decision/body.
scenarios.expected: Authorized identical retries return the recorded outcome without duplicate effects. Reusing a key for changed intent conflicts and cannot alter the original decision.
scenarios.assessment: Repeated same-key exact replay and same-key opposite-decision conflict passed; one command/history result preserved.

scenarios.scenario: Membership revocation or Owner-to-Staff demotion commits between session resolution and a protected write from an already-open tab.
scenarios.expected: A protected write must not rely on a stale role snapshot after revocation wins. Enforce the current membership at the mutation boundary and invalidate subsequent privileged actions.
scenarios.assessment: Revocation at protected catalog/Order write boundaries passed. Owner-to-Staff demotion at the boundary was not independently injected.

scenarios.scenario: Staff paginates/searches an inbox containing many other assignments; a cursor copied from Owner or Store B is submitted as Staff.
scenarios.expected: Every page and filtered summary uses current Store and assignment visibility. A foreign/tampered cursor cannot broaden access; do not reveal other users’ counts or use stale authorization embedded in a cursor.
scenarios.assessment: Sparse Staff visibility, filtering and principal-bound cursor tests passed. Copied Owner and Store-B cursor variants were not independently replayed.

scenarios.scenario: Assigned inbox has zero Orders, one Order, exactly a page, and one more than a page; the last item is reassigned away between requests.
scenarios.expected: Empty/next/previous states remain usable and current counts reflect authorized rows. No inaccessible phantom detail or permanent pagination trap after reassignment.
scenarios.assessment: Zero/one assigned Order and pagination behavior covered. Exact 25/26 plus reassignment of the final visible item was not independently replayed.

scenarios.scenario: A large populated Store is queried with a sparse Staff assignment and payment-reference search.
scenarios.expected: Scope/filter before pagination, use bounded requests, and keep summaries server-derived. Planning must define a representative volume and latency target; no performance pass is claimed without measurement.
scenarios.assessment: 10,000 Orders/200 assignments: domain list p95 Staff 17ms, Owner 17ms. Raw customer-name search 2ms vs 1ms exceeds proposed 1.25x relative budget; payment-reference search is not measured. No full scenario pass claimed.

scenarios.scenario: Automated clients send repeated invalid sign-ins and public Order submissions while Owner and Staff are working.
scenarios.expected: Use the selected auth library’s configured abuse controls and preserve existing public input/idempotency limits. Return explicit bounded failures rather than unbounded work or private fallback; public access must not require a Console session.
scenarios.assessment: Repeated invalid social sign-in reaches 429 with Retry-After and no sessions. Mixed public-Order abuse while Owner/Staff work was not load-tested.

scenarios.scenario: Owner A signs out and Staff B signs in in the same browser while an old A detail request is still in flight; the user also uses Back.
scenarios.expected: Clear A private state and discard old-generation responses. B must not see A content resurrected by a response, client cache, or restored page; fresh requests enforce B scope.
scenarios.assessment: Real browser held Owner-A response, switched to Staff-B, released response, used Back: no old Owner evidence restored; crossed Product read 404.

scenarios.scenario: A formerly assigned Staff member replays a previously successful command key after reassignment or session expiry.
scenarios.expected: Check present identity and resource authorization before looking up/returning a stored result. Do not leak the old result or repeat its effect; existing durable history remains intact.
scenarios.assessment: Replayed command authorization after assignment/session loss passed existing integration and browser contracts.

scenarios.scenario: After rejection, Customer and Console-on-behalf both try another Refund submission; repeat after approval.
scenarios.expected: Both paths retain the original request and final decision, with no second request or renewed pending state. Authorized submission retries return the recorded request; conflicting decisions remain refused.
scenarios.assessment: Real Customer resubmission after approval/rejection preserves terminal outcome and no new form. Console-on-behalf terminal resubmission was not independently replayed.

scenarios.scenario: Caller requests a Refund on pending/canceled Order or tries to decide an absent/already-decided request.
scenarios.expected: Enforce Order and request state independently from role. Invalid transitions have no effect; a terminal decision cannot be reopened or flipped through another endpoint.
scenarios.assessment: Invalid Order/refund transitions and absent/already-final decision requests rejected by existing domain/HTTP tests.

scenarios.scenario: At 375 px, long person/Store names and Refund messages appear with assignment controls and sign-out navigation.
scenarios.expected: No horizontal page scroll or hidden primary action. Preserve existing tokenized accent fill/ink, readable state labels, and Products/Orders navigation only.
scenarios.assessment: Console detail document width 547 on a 375 viewport with long Unicode assignee name. Enabled primary action fill/text match color-accent/color-accent-ink.

scenarios.scenario: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user signs in, selects an assignee, confirms Reject, and encounters a server denial.
scenarios.expected: Controls have clear names; focus reaches and returns from dialogs; errors and final outcomes are announced. Pending states prevent accidental duplicate intent without trapping focus.
scenarios.assessment: Real keyboard Approve/Reject actions passed, plus existing keyboard contracts. Actual screen-reader announcements and the entire sign-in/assignment/denial flow with assistive technology not verified.

scenarios.scenario: Local localhost and 127.0.0.1 configurations or deployed HTTPS origins differ; the browser blocks or does not send the session cookie.
scenarios.expected: Show a recoverable sign-in failure, never anonymous private access. Verify real cookie/trusted-origin settings for each supported environment without relaxing them globally.
scenarios.assessment: Fresh 127.0.0.1 and localhost browser auth/cookie checks passed. Deployed HTTPS cookie/origin behavior not exercised.

scenarios.scenario: Connectivity drops during sign-in, assignment, or approval and the browser reloads before the response is known.
scenarios.expected: Do not announce success from local intent or queue a new privileged mutation automatically. Restore current server state after reconnect and reconcile any authorized retry with the original command identity.
scenarios.assessment: Existing unknown-outcome recovery contracts passed. Reload during unresolved sign-in/assignment/approval with original intent/key continuity not independently exercised.

scenarios.scenario: The auth/session or membership lookup fails because D1 is unavailable while public assets remain served.
scenarios.expected: Private operations fail closed with a recoverable service error. No bootstrap Owner, cached-role bypass, or implicit Store A fallback; no private payload in the error.
scenarios.assessment: Session-table and additional membership-table outages fail closed with 503/service_unavailable rather than anonymous access; membership outage preserves session row.

scenarios.scenario: Fault injection fails a statement between assignment/decision persistence, audit insertion, and command-ledger recording.
scenarios.expected: Rollback the entire domain mutation. The observable result is all committed once or none committed, not a decision without attribution or a success ledger without its business effect.
scenarios.assessment: Assignment and decision batch-boundary fault injection passes with atomic rollback of assignment/decision, audit and command records.

scenarios.scenario: An Owner delivery-file upload reaches R2 but its Store-scoped database association fails, or an unauthorized Staff upload attempts to reach R2.
scenarios.expected: Authorize before consuming/uploading the private mutation. On association failure preserve old references and snapshots; compensate only the new unreferenced object, never another Store’s or a purchased object.
scenarios.assessment: R2 cleanup after failed association and Staff rejection before unauthorized catalog/R2 writes passed.

scenarios.scenario: A populated schema migration fails, or the old anonymous Worker continues writing during the identity/schema cutover.
scenarios.expected: A rehearsed writer barrier/checkpoint prevents mixed-writer corruption. Stop the cutover on failure; do not roll back to an anonymous/incompatible writer or reset data to make migration pass. Preserve public service outside the explicitly controlled cutover window.
scenarios.assessment: Real isolated raw-Wrangler populated migration failure/reapply and preservation rehearsal passed. A live old anonymous writer during a real cutover was not exercised; remote untouched.

scenarios.scenario: Owner B and Staff B submit known Store A IDs, slugs, Order references, Variant IDs, and delivery-file targets to every private read/write/preview/import path.
scenarios.expected: All paths enforce Store scope before returning private resource or validation details. Return unavailable/not-found for out-of-scope resources; no R2 side effect or cross-Store mutation.
scenarios.assessment: Foreign-Store Product/Order/file/preview/import isolation passed. Full explicit cross-Store Variant-ID matrix was not independently replayed.

scenarios.scenario: Assigned Staff calls Refund decision, assignment, Product edit, CSV import, delivery-file PUT/DELETE, or schema replacement directly without using the UI.
scenarios.expected: The central evaluator refuses every Owner-only action. Alternative methods and indirect removal paths cannot bypass read-only Products or Owner-only decisions; unsupported deletion APIs remain unsupported.
scenarios.assessment: Assigned Staff Owner-only actions denied by existing suites; extra direct file DELETE, schema replacement and Product mutation probes return 403.

scenarios.scenario: A guessed capability, another Order’s valid capability, and a Customer capability sent to Console routes are tested, including alongside an unrelated valid Console cookie.
scenarios.expected: Private Customer access requires the exact matching capability. Console requires its own identity and membership; neither credential upgrades the other or broadens resource scope. No-match responses reveal no private Order data.
scenarios.assessment: Wrong/other Order capabilities and unrelated Console-cookie boundaries passed existing tests; extra capability-only Console request 401 and guessed Customer capability 404.

scenarios.scenario: A malicious origin submits cookie-bearing Console mutations and probes auth trusted-origin/CORS handling, including missing or null Origin variants.
scenarios.expected: A defined CSRF policy rejects unauthorized browser-origin mutations before effects. Do not treat CORS as authorization or add wildcard credentialed origins; preserve the explicitly supported first-party request forms.
scenarios.assessment: Exact trusted Origin, malicious/missing/null Origin and Fetch Metadata/CORS denial cases passed locally.

scenarios.scenario: Staff A1 knows an unassigned Store A Order reference and another Order assigned to A2; calls detail, payment, fulfill, cancel, and Refund submission directly.
scenarios.expected: Same-Store membership is insufficient: deny private detail and every mutation on both Orders without disclosing their Customer/payment fields or writing a command ledger. Owner can still read and assign them.
scenarios.assessment: Extra HTTP matrix: unassigned and other-Staff-assigned detail/payment/fulfill/cancel/refund all 404; no command/history mutation.

scenarios.scenario: Run the forward migration against a populated S1–S3 fixture containing Variants, old Customer capabilities, pending Refunds, manual payments, and legacy paid Orders.
scenarios.expected: Compare pre/post records and relationships: preserve IDs, totals, references, hashes, snapshots, history, and retained R2 keys under store_nexus. Create no fabricated payments, fulfillment, or replacement Store A.
scenarios.assessment: Fresh Node22 raw-Wrangler populated S1-S3 migration/provisioning rehearsal and preservation checks passed.

scenarios.scenario: Historical events have null actor IDs and legacy source/contract values; new user foreign keys and decision event checks are introduced.
scenarios.expected: Preserve truthful legacy provenance without assigning the new Owner to past anonymous activity. New authenticated events have real actors; old event constraints/references survive the migration.
scenarios.assessment: Legacy null actor/source/contract records and new schema constraints passed migration and acceptance suites.

scenarios.scenario: Assignment targets a nonexistent user, Owner rather than Staff, removed Staff, or Staff in Store B; a direct persistence attempt links a Refund/history record across Stores.
scenarios.expected: Application rules and appropriate relational constraints reject invalid references. Never leave a valid-looking assignment to an ineligible membership or cross-Store aggregate link.
scenarios.assessment: Invalid assignment targets and cross-Store constraints covered. Explicit direct Refund/history cross-Store link variants were not independently replayed.

scenarios.scenario: Store B provisioning is run twice and uses Product slugs/SKUs matching Store A; generated record IDs or account identifiers collide.
scenarios.expected: Provisioning is repeat-safe or fails explicitly without changing A. Store-scoped slugs/SKUs may coexist; global ID collisions cannot overwrite existing rows, credentials, or memberships.
scenarios.assessment: Repeated/conflicting provisioning and Store-local slug behavior covered. Full matching-SKU and generated-record-ID collision combination was not independently replayed.

scenarios.scenario: The selected Better Auth version/adapter works in Node but is exercised in the actual Workers runtime across sign-in, get-session, expiry, and sign-out.
scenarios.expected: The real D1-backed session lifecycle works with supported runtime APIs and migration ownership. An incompatible adapter blocks integration rather than falling back to an in-memory/demo identity.
scenarios.assessment: Pinned Better Auth real Worker/D1 session lifecycle and browser session behavior passed. Browser fixtures provision local sessions; no external Google OAuth login claimed.

scenarios.scenario: A cached pre-S4 Console sends old headers/payloads or invokes former bootstrap paths after cutover.
scenarios.expected: Old clients cannot retain anonymous private access. Authentication precedes private disclosure/replay; incompatible requests receive a recoverable contract error or login requirement without side effects.
scenarios.assessment: Legacy contract headers/payloads and obsolete bootstrap/account-creation paths fail closed in current tests.

scenarios.scenario: A browser signed into Store B opens the public Storefront, reads Products, and submits an Order with a forged Store field.
scenarios.expected: The public Storefront remains explicitly Store A. Ignore/reject unsupported routing fields rather than deriving Store from the Console cookie; create only the intended A Order and expose no private B data.
scenarios.assessment: Store-B Console identity does not select public Store; extra public Order forged storeId returns 422 without an Order write.

scenarios.scenario: Approve and Reject results travel through domain, API client types, Console detail, and existing private Customer page; an old pending request is opened after deployment.
scenarios.expected: Every layer reads the same persisted state and renders supported statuses. No pending-only type/parser drops decisions; existing pending requests remain usable and Customer output stays separate from Console output.
scenarios.assessment: Real paid/approve, fulfilled/approve and paid/reject flows render terminal status in Console and Customer page after reload; old pending preservation covered separately by migration tests, not remote deployment.

scenarios.scenario: Compare Customer and public responses before/after assignment and decision when Console holds person names, history, notes, and payment evidence.
scenarios.expected: An explicit Customer-safe projection includes the relevant decision but excludes Staff/Owner identity, internal notes/history, delivery configuration, and Console-only payment evidence. Public catalog reveals none of the private Order.
scenarios.assessment: Public/Customer projection privacy contracts passed; internal payment/history/person evidence remains private.

scenarios.scenario: An auth or capability lookup fails and diagnostic logs, error bodies, analytics hooks, or copied URLs could capture credentials.
scenarios.expected: Do not log session cookies, passwords, raw capabilities, private Order URLs, or unnecessary Customer PII. Keep the capability in its existing fragment/header channel and errors safe to share.
scenarios.assessment: Existing redaction/private-artifact checks and extra membership outage cookie/log probe passed. Exhaustive auth/capability failure logs, analytics and copied-URL audit not performed.

scenarios.scenario: The deciding Owner later changes display name or loses membership; an auditor opens the old decision.
scenarios.expected: The durable decision retains its real actor identity and timestamp without rewriting history or confusing it with the requester. No account-deletion UI is required; provenance must survive supported identity changes.
scenarios.assessment: Stable deciding actor/history survives display-name change and membership loss in acceptance tests.

scenarios.scenario: Owner replaces/removes catalog delivery content after an earlier purchase while a Refund remains approved but unexecuted.
scenarios.expected: Preserve the purchased immutable snapshot and referenced private object under existing retention rules. S4 approval must not trigger file destruction, access revocation, or a claim of completed reversal.
scenarios.assessment: Purchased delivery snapshot retention after catalog replacement/removal and non-executing refund approval invariants passed complementary suites; not claimed as one combined remote journey.

scenarios.scenario: Owner assigns a pending Order to Staff; Staff records its manual payment, then fulfills it, and attempts cancellation after payment.
scenarios.expected: Valid assigned processing succeeds with the real Staff actor and existing ledger/transition rules. Invalid cancellation fails even though Staff remains assigned; the Customer sees the corresponding safe Order state.
scenarios.assessment: Real assigned Staff records manual payment and fulfills; cancellation after payment rejected 409.

scenarios.scenario: Owner approves a Refund for a paid Order and separately for a fulfilled Order, then both apps reload.
scenarios.expected: Refund is approved and awaiting execution; each Order retains its prior paid/fulfilled status. No payment reversal, refunded status, S5 job execution, or implied money movement occurs.
scenarios.assessment: Real paid and fulfilled approvals preserve Order status and exact payment snapshot; Console and Customer page retain final outcome after reload.

scenarios.scenario: A legacy paid Order has no original payment ledger evidence, and Owner decides its Refund Request.
scenarios.expected: The S4 decision can be recorded without inventing a payment source/reference. Preserve the legacy evidence gap for S5; neither UI promises automatic repayment nor migration manufactures evidence.
scenarios.assessment: Legacy paid Order without payment ledger can receive refund decision without inventing payment/refund evidence.

scenarios.scenario: An Owner uses a permitted removal operation against protected referenced data, or Staff tries an equivalent removal through another mutation.
scenarios.expected: Owner authority does not bypass existing snapshot/FK retention guards. Staff read-only/Owner-only rules cover indirect mutation paths; do not add new destructive APIs solely to demonstrate denial.
scenarios.assessment: Protected referenced-content removal/retention checks passed. Complete equivalent Staff indirect-mutation removal matrix not independently replayed.

scope.temporaryProbes: Throwaway probe files and isolated state removed after recording results; commands above describe executed evidence, not retained new tests.
